name: MONA deferred pair burn applied after the pool is bought out
summary: Every MONA sale into the MONA/USDT pair is recorded in BurnAddress.sellMona, and the next ordinary transfer by anyone makes BurnAddress.burn() call monaToken.burnsellMona(sellMona - burnedMona), which burns that amount from the pair and syncs, whatever the pair's reserves are by then. Buys whose recipient is excluded from transfer rules skip _handleBuy, so its burn-threshold check (7.10m of 13m burned, which blocked ordinary buys) and its 1/33-of-reserve limit do not apply. The attacker borrowed USDT on Venus against flash-loaned WBNB, bought 25 LisaVault nodes through fresh helper contracts to obtain 10,000 MONA, sold 9,900 MONA (7,641.13 reaching the pair and queued for burning), then swapped 86.03m USDT into the pair for its 9,875,067 MONA with the excluded deployer 0xdd0215b5 as recipient, leaving 7,641.13 MONA plus dust. A zero transfer triggered the queued burn of 7,641.13 MONA from the pair, leaving 1e-8 MONA against 86.09m USDT, and a 94 MONA sale took the whole USDT reserve, including the pool's original 66,450.31 USDT.
notes: Reset is monaToken.setBurnAddress(0xd7ab8cc9) (burnAddress(), block 92226123), which gave the BurnAddress contract the right to burn MONA from the pair through burnsellMona; it follows the token's deployment (92222415, which also created the pair and excluded the deployer) and BurnAddress's deployment (92225964). Later writes are openTrade() (trading switch, packed into the same slot as burnAddress; pause state, rule 8), setJoinAddress (joinAddress 0xbb79573f, not executed by the anchor) and balance changes.

The LisaVault node contract 0xaea6e5ca only supplied the MONA the attacker sold: each 220 USDT node paid 400 MONA, and the 25 helper contracts were needed because MONA cannot be bought from the pair by ordinary addresses before the burn threshold. The DeFiHackLabs PoC's 'insider LP removal' stage is not what the anchor did: no LP tokens moved; the 66,450 USDT left through the swap after the queued burn.

No earlier exploit: the pair's first USDT outflows ever are the two swaps of the anchor (51.25 and 86,092,750.64 USDT); before it the pool only received USDT from the deployer and the join contracts 0xc4ec26eb/0xbb79573f. After the anchor 0.0092 USDT remained, so no repeat was possible. The attacker's earlier transactions (bindReferrer, join calls, one buyNode at block 92415493) are preparation.

Loss is the pair's USDT (66,450.31, priced $66,468.71 by loss.mjs). The 9,874,973 MONA the pair lost went to the excluded deployer 0xdd0215b5 (the swap recipient the attacker named) or were burned; the attacker realised nothing from them, so they are valued at 0 (rule 12). The attacker's net take was 60,950.31 USDT after paying 25 x 220 USDT for nodes.
